note: Alaska U.S. Senate and governor races, researched Oct. 25, 2026.

candidates.name: Mary Peltola
candidates.bio: U.S. representative for Alaska's at-large district from 2022 to 2025 and the first Alaska Native elected to Congress.

source.title: U.S. House roll call 513 (2022) on the Respect for Marriage Act (H.R. 8404): Peltola voted Yea
U.S. House roll call 151 (2024) on H.R. 8035, military aid for Ukraine: Peltola voted Yea
U.S. House roll call 152 (2024) on H.R. 8034, military aid for Israel: Peltola voted Yea
guides.vote, 2026 Alaska U.S. Senate voters guide: Peltola supports Medicaid coverage of abortion and opposes a national ban (Alaska Beacon, 2024)
source.quote: I will always protect the right to choose.

source.title: guides.vote, 2026 Alaska U.S. Senate voters guide: Peltola opposes a national abortion ban (Alaska Beacon, 2024); her campaign said a 2022 remark backing a 16-week limit was a mistake
guides.vote, 2026 Alaska U.S. Senate voters guide: Peltola would fight to restore federal tax credits for solar, wind and hydropower projects
guides.vote, 2026 Alaska U.S. Senate voters guide: Peltola supports oil and gas development alongside renewables (campaign energy plan)
guides.vote, 2026 Alaska U.S. Senate voters guide: Peltola voted against repealing greenhouse gas reduction programs (H.R. 1023; House roll call 104, 2024)

guides.vote, 2026 Alaska U.S. Senate voters guide: Peltola voted against overturning the rule extending Clean Water Act protection to more streams and wetlands (H.J.Res. 27; House roll call 187, 2023)
guides.vote, 2026 Alaska U.S. Senate voters guide: Peltola calls for more funding for local law enforcement
source.quote: more funding for local law enforcement

source.title: guides.vote, 2026 Alaska U.S. Senate voters guide: Peltola would raise taxes on millionaires and billionaires to end federal income tax for people earning under $92,000
guides.vote, 2026 Alaska U.S. Senate voters guide: Peltola would end federal income tax for people earning under $92,000, paid for by taxing millionaires and billionaires
guides.vote, 2026 Alaska U.S. Senate voters guide: Peltola would shift income taxes from people earning under $92,000 to millionaires and billionaires
guides.vote, 2026 Alaska U.S. Senate voters guide: Peltola would restore the Medicaid funding cut by the 2025 budget law
source.quote: We can restore Medicaid and the [ACA] tax credits

source.title: guides.vote, 2026 Alaska U.S. Senate voters guide: Peltola would restore the ACA premium tax credits
guides.vote, 2026 Alaska U.S. Senate voters guide: Peltola on health coverage
source.quote: Every Alaskan should be able to access and afford healthcare.

source.title: guides.vote, 2026 Alaska U.S. Senate voters guide: Peltola cosponsored the Dignity Act (H.R. 3599), pairing border security with a path to legal status, including for Dreamers
guides.vote, 2026 Alaska U.S. Senate voters guide: Peltola voted for H.Res. 957 denouncing the Biden administration's border policies (2024) and cosponsored the Dignity Act's border security measures
guides.vote, 2026 Alaska U.S. Senate voters guide: Peltola says presidents should not act alone on major decisions (Alaska Beacon, May 2026)
source.quote: There is a need for the War Powers Act.

source.title: guides.vote, 2026 Alaska U.S. Senate voters guide: Peltola says the war in Iran is driving up gas and diesel prices
guides.vote, 2026 Alaska U.S. Senate voters guide: Peltola cosponsored the PRO Act (H.R. 20, 2023) to protect organizing and collective bargaining
guides.vote, 2026 Alaska U.S. Senate voters guide: Peltola supported the Equality Act's ban on discrimination by sexual orientation and gender identity
guides.vote, 2026 Alaska U.S. Senate voters guide: Peltola voted against banning transgender students from girls' school sports (H.R. 734; House roll call 192, 2023), calling the ban bullying
guides.vote, 2026 Alaska U.S. Senate voters guide: Peltola backs livable wages and tax incentives for companies that pay fair wages
source.quote: The best wage is one that's livable.

source.title: guides.vote, 2026 Alaska U.S. Senate voters guide: Peltola supports ranked-choice voting

candidates.name: Dan S. Sullivan
candidates.bio: U.S. senator since 2015, a Marine Corps Reserve officer and a former Alaska attorney general.

source.title: guides.vote, 2026 Alaska U.S. Senate voters guide: Sullivan cosponsored S. 6, the Born-Alive Abortion Survivors Protection Act
source.quote: I'm as pro-life as they come.

source.title: guides.vote, 2026 Alaska U.S. Senate voters guide: Sullivan supported overturning Roe v. Wade and returning abortion law to the states
guides.vote, 2026 Alaska U.S. Senate voters guide: Sullivan voted against the 2022 clean energy investments (Senate roll call 325) and to end the clean energy tax credits (Senate roll call 372, 2025)
guides.vote, 2026 Alaska U.S. Senate voters guide: Sullivan on energy

guides.vote, 2026 Alaska U.S. Senate voters guide: Sullivan cosponsored S.J.Res. 31 to undo limits on seven hazardous air pollutants and voted to overturn the Clean Water Act streams and wetlands rule (Senate roll call 79, 2023)

guides.vote, 2026 Alaska U.S. Senate voters guide: Sullivan introduced bills making assault on a public safety officer a federal crime (S. 1766) and ending the statute of limitations for fatal overdose crimes (S. 4209)
guides.vote, 2026 Alaska U.S. Senate voters guide: Sullivan opposes reckless federal spending and voted to cancel public broadcasting funding (Senate roll call 411, 2025)
guides.vote, 2026 Alaska U.S. Senate voters guide: Sullivan voted for the 2025 law that cut Medicaid (Senate roll call 372), after negotiating rural health funding in it

guides.vote, 2026 Alaska U.S. Senate voters guide: Sullivan voted to extend ACA premium tax credits for three years (Senate roll call 644, 2025) but wants the subsidies tapered down rather than ended abruptly
guides.vote, 2026 Alaska U.S. Senate voters guide: Sullivan cosponsored S. 2824 to build 900 miles of border wall and limit asylum
guides.vote, 2026 Alaska U.S. Senate voters guide: Sullivan cosponsored S. 2824, which requires E-Verify for new hires
guides.vote, 2026 Alaska U.S. Senate voters guide: Sullivan voted for $75 billion more for ICE (2025) and $70 billion more for DHS (2026), while saying ICE should revise its tactics
guides.vote, 2026 Alaska U.S. Senate voters guide: Sullivan voted five times in 2026 against requiring congressional authorization for military action in Iran
guides.vote, 2026 Alaska U.S. Senate voters guide: Sullivan on Iran (2025)
source.quote: I fully support the President and his national security team

source.title: guides.vote, 2026 Alaska U.S. Senate voters guide: Sullivan voted for the Respect for Marriage Act, citing its religious liberty protections (Senate roll call 362, 2022), after opposing the 2015 Supreme Court ruling
guides.vote, 2026 Alaska U.S. Senate voters guide: Sullivan signed a 2022 letter opposing proposed federal protections for transgender athletes
guides.vote, 2026 Alaska U.S. Senate voters guide: Sullivan voted against a $15 federal minimum wage (Senate roll call 74, 2021)
guides.vote, 2026 Alaska U.S. Senate voters guide: Sullivan voted to extend the 2017 tax cuts (2025) and against raising taxes on corporations and the wealthy (Senate roll call 357, 2021)
guides.vote, 2026 Alaska U.S. Senate voters guide: Sullivan supports the SAVE Act's proof-of-citizenship requirement for voter registration (Alaska Current, Feb. 2026)
guides.vote, 2026 Alaska U.S. Senate voters guide: Sullivan voted against the 2021 voting access bill (S. 2093) and the John Lewis Voting Rights Act (S. 4)

candidates.name: Jonathan Kreiss-Tomkins
candidates.bio: Alaska state representative from Sitka from 2013 to 2023.

source.title: Alaska Beacon, Sept. 22, 2026: Kreiss-Tomkins voted against abortion limits for 10 years in the Alaska House and would uphold the state Supreme Court's rulings
source.quote: Medical privacy and reproductive freedom should be fundamental personal freedoms

source.title: Alaska Beacon, Sept. 22, 2026: Kreiss-Tomkins voted in 2014 against limiting abortion to cases of rape, incest or medical necessity
Alaska Beacon, Oct. 9, 2026: Kreiss-Tomkins opposes lowering the voter-approved minimum wage, which rises to $15 in 2027
Alaska Beacon, Oct. 12, 2026: Kreiss-Tomkins would aim to expand paid family leave
Alaska Beacon, Oct. 12, 2026: Kreiss-Tomkins supports recurring state child care funding, child care workforce investment and a long-term goal of universal pre-K
Alaska's News Source debate report, Oct. 8, 2026: Kreiss-Tomkins's first bill would fund K-12 schools a year in advance, and he would raise school funding
Alaska Public Media debate report, Oct. 9, 2026: Kreiss-Tomkins would boost public school funding
Alaska's News Source debate report, Oct. 8, 2026: Kreiss-Tomkins backs streamlined permitting for a statewide housing building boom
Alaska's News Source debate report, Oct. 8, 2026: Kreiss-Tomkins supports an all-of-the-above energy approach, a gas line and royalty relief for Cook Inlet gas producers
Alaska's News Source debate report, Oct. 8, 2026: Kreiss-Tomkins would make the oil company Hilcorp pay state corporate income tax, calling its exemption unfair

candidates.name: Bernadette Wilson
candidates.bio: Anchorage business owner and talk radio host.

source.title: Alaska Beacon, Sept. 22, 2026: Wilson would appoint a pro-life advocate in her administration and have her attorney general narrow medically necessary abortion care
Alaska Beacon, Sept. 22, 2026: Wilson would keep fighting the state Supreme Court over abortion restrictions and run a state campaign on the risks of medication abortion
Alaska Beacon, Oct. 9, 2026: Wilson supports repealing the voter-approved minimum wage increases and paid sick leave law
Alaska's News Source debate report, Oct. 8, 2026: Wilson calls a gas line the biggest lever for lower energy costs
source.quote: been a terrible business partner to our oil and gas industries

source.title: Alaska's News Source debate report, Oct. 8, 2026: Wilson backs vocational training aligned with workforce needs
Alaska Public Media debate report, Oct. 9, 2026: Wilson would not raise school funding without a clear plan to improve student performance

candidates.name: Dave Bronson
candidates.bio: Mayor of Anchorage from 2021 to 2024 and a cofounder of the anti-abortion group Alaska Family Action.

source.title: Alaska Beacon, Sept. 22, 2026: Bronson would veto any state money for abortion
source.quote: He vetoes any bit of money, any funding that goes towards abortion

source.title: Alaska Beacon, Sept. 22, 2026: Bronson would fight the state Supreme Court over abortion and replace merit selection of judges with elections
Alaska Beacon, Oct. 9, 2026: Bronson would repeal the voter-approved minimum wage increase and paid sick leave
source.quote: Mandatory sick leave, minimum wage — I would repeal them both

source.title: Alaska Beacon, Oct. 12, 2026: Bronson supports recurring state child care funding and calls child care essential infrastructure
Alaska's News Source debate report, Oct. 8, 2026: Bronson blames federal regulation for stalled resource development and wants a second Cook Inlet drilling rig

candidates.name: Treg Taylor
candidates.bio: Former Alaska attorney general under Gov. Mike Dunleavy.

source.title: Alaska Beacon, Sept. 22, 2026: As attorney general, Taylor sought to restrict the abortion pill mifepristone (2023) and defended limits on telehealth prescriptions
Alaska Beacon, Sept. 22, 2026: Taylor openly opposes abortion and worked to restrict it as attorney general
Alaska Public Media debate report, Oct. 9, 2026: Taylor helped pass the law letting fentanyl dealers be charged with murder in overdose deaths
Alaska's News Source debate report, Oct. 8, 2026: Taylor's first bill would fund K-12 schools a year in advance, with accountability restored to the Alaska Reads Act
Alaska's News Source debate report, Oct. 8, 2026: Taylor backs vocational training aligned with workforce needs
Alaska Beacon, Oct. 12, 2026: Taylor would expand child care through federal funds, tax credits and fewer regulations rather than new state money, and opposes statewide pre-K
Alaska's News Source debate report, Oct. 8, 2026: Taylor defended the Willow oil project and cites the jobs a gas line would bring
